scenes.title: Prefect (Flows & Tasks)
scenes.narration: This lesson introduces Prefect, an orchestrator that lets you turn ordinary Python functions into observable, resilient workflows with minimal ceremony.

scenes.title: Prefect's core idea
bullets: A flow is a workflow; a task is a step
You add decorators to normal Python functions
The DAG emerges from how functions call each other
scenes.narration: Prefect's central idea is that your workflow is just Python. A flow represents an entire workflow while a task represents a single step, and you create them simply by adding decorators to ordinary functions. There is no separate graph to declare, because the dependency structure emerges naturally from how your functions call one another at runtime.

scenes.title: A Prefect flow
scenes.narration: This complete pipeline shows how little ceremony Prefect requires. The task decorator turns extract and transform into tracked steps, and the flow decorator turns etl into an orchestrated workflow. Prefect observes that transform is called with extract's result and infers the dependency for you. Notice the retries argument on extract: with a single parameter it will retry three times with a delay, giving you resilience for free on flaky external calls.

scenes.title: Prefect versus classic Airflow

left.heading: Prefect
points: Run anywhere, then attach a server later
Rich retries and caching built in

right.heading: Airflow
points: Declarative DAGs parsed on a schedule

scenes.narration: Prefect and Airflow make different trade-offs. Prefect flows are dynamic and Python-native, run anywhere including your laptop, and you can attach a Prefect server for scheduling and observability afterward. Airflow takes a more declarative approach with DAGs parsed on a schedule around a central scheduler and metadata database, backed by an enormous ecosystem of provider integrations. Prefect often feels lighter for Python-heavy teams, while Airflow's maturity suits large standardized platforms.

scenes.title: What Prefect adds around your code
bullets: Deployments for scheduling and remote runs
scenes.narration: Beyond running your functions, Prefect wraps them with production features. It tracks the state of every task and surfaces it in a UI, it provides retries, timeouts, and caching of results so unchanged work is skipped, and it offers deployments that let you schedule flows and run them on remote infrastructure. You get these capabilities by decorating code rather than rewriting it.

scenes.text: Prefect turns plain Python functions into resilient, observable workflows with decorators, making it a natural fit for Python-first data teams.
scenes.narration: The key point is that Prefect turns plain Python functions into resilient, observable workflows through simple decorators, which makes it an especially natural fit for Python-first data teams that want orchestration without heavy boilerplate.
